speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development since the announcement of the increase in childcare subsidies (a) how many childcare operators have raised their fees; (b) what is the increase quantum; and (c) how much savings can be expected, taking into account the increment and subsidies.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development how does the Government intend to assist parents who will not benefit from the recent increase in Government childcare subsidies, to cope with childcare fee hikes by the 220 childcare centres as well as possibly other childcare centres.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The number of centres increasing fees in 2020 is broadly comparable to previous years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: From time to time, preschools adjust their fees to keep up with operational costs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But most manage their fee increases, in order to remain competitive.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, with the large number of operators, every year some operator or other will make some adjustments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: All preschools are required to inform parents and the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) of any increase in fees by 1 September of the preceding year, so that parents can make an informed choice about their child’s preschool.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Of the centres raising fees next year, a large majority had informed ECDA even before subsidy enhancements were announced at the National Day Rally.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Among some of the centres raising fees are those run by Anchor Operators and Partner Operators.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are centres operating below the stipulated fee caps, which have been maintained at their current levels since 2014 for Anchor Operators and 2016 for Partner Operators.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The industry median fees have thus remained unchanged at $856 since 2016.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, in 2021, we will lower fee caps for Partner Operator centres when their new five-year term begins, further reducing industry median fees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With enhanced childcare subsidies from January 2020, the majority of working families will pay less for childcare, even with the fee adjustment in one-fifth of the childcare centres.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Allow me to illustrate what working families will pay for full-day childcare at an Anchor Operator preschool with the enhanced subsidies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Suppose the fees are below fee cap, say $740, and an increase by 5% to the fee cap of $770 next January, after the Goods and Services Tax (GST).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They pay $40 per month at this preschool today; from January next year, they will pay $3 per month.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They pay $340 per month today; from January next year, they will pay $130.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They pay $440 per month today; from January next year, they will pay $280 per month.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As you can see, preschool expenses should fall for most families receiving Additional Subsidy, even with the fee increase in one-fifth of the childcare centres.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They do not apply only to Anchor Operator or Partner Operator childcare centres.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For families with non-working mothers or those who are earning more than $12,000 a month and hence do not qualify for the enhanced Additional Subsidy, we provide additional help for those who need it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, if the mother is not working because she is providing full-time care for a younger child aged 24 months and below, or is looking for employment, she may qualify for higher subsidies under Special Approval.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Low-income families who face difficulties paying their monthly childcare fees even after subsidies may also apply for financial assistance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over the next few years, parents will increasingly have more affordable and quality preschool options to choose from, as we increase the number of Anchor Operator and Partner Operator preschools, and a few more Ministry of Education (MOE) Kindergartens.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: By around 2025, the share of Anchor Operator, Partner Operator and MOE preschool places will rise to 80%, up from just over 50% today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the medium term, as Government-supported preschools grow and come under the stipulated fee caps, we will lower their fee caps so that parents will pay around the equivalent of primary school fees plus after-school student care fees for full-day preschool, before means-tested subsidies kick in.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These enhancements will more than double annual Government spending on preschool, from $1 billion today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are committed and will continue to make quality preschool more affordable and accessible to give every child a good start in life.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: In fact, many of us have received feedback from our residents.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: They have given comments that every time the Government increases subsidies, the childcare operators will increase their fees, and it seems to be corresponding.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: But I thank the Minister for producing the data as well as the statistics which are very important.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: It is still quite tough for middle-income families which have a few children in childcare centres, especially for those who, even with the subsidy itself, may find it tough with their monthly incomes.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The other group that I am a little bit concerned about is the non-working mothers.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I understand there is already additional subsidy for non-working mothers if they fulfil the criteria.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: My question is, currently, how many of these children who enjoy the subsidies are children of non-working mothers?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Can we equalise both groups, instead of making them apply to these criteria?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If we were to put working mothers or non-working mothers aside, how much more increase in terms of subsidies would the Government have to bear, rather than make the non-working mothers go and apply for additional subsidies?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Every year, some preschool operators will make some adjustments to their fees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are many operators – private, not-for profit, as well as MOE Kindergartens.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, every year, there will be some adjustments, whether or not we make adjustments to our subsidies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are, of course, some centres, private operators, that charge, say thousands of dollars in fees that make adjustments in the hundreds of dollars.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that is on the Member's first question.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The second point is on families with many children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On non-working mothers, the support provided to them takes into account the fact that because they are working, they will need full-day childcare.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: By "working mother", we are talking about working two days a week, and that can include the informal sector as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We do grant special approval if mothers have caregiving needs for children younger than 24 months or if they are looking after other dependants.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For those who are looking for employment, we make concessions for them and allow them to benefit from the full subsidy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And for those who are non-working mothers, what they can do is, they can go for the basic subsidy for full-day childcare, or if not and they are at home with no other caregiving responsibilities other than their young children, then, there is the option to go for kindergarten with Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme subsidies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, for half a day, they get pedagogical support; the other half a day, time with the parents, time with the family, family-bonding time.
